summary: MCP launcher, runtime diagnostic, dispatch-readiness, and validation-run tools.

tools.display_name: Workspace Chassis Control Engine admission runtime diagnostic
tools.notes: Read-only agent-safe MCP route that diagnoses the running MCP server process (not the caller shell) for Chassis Control Engine worker_admission_v1 runtime config. Reports only source names and booleans (service URL, API key, worker-admission route, request-contract digest presence, and whether the remote-admission observability path is loaded); never returns any secret value, route value, digest, key hash, bearer material, project id, or request/response body.

Read-only introspection for the dispatch caller/session identity and bootstrap review contract. Identity authority must be launcher- or transport-minted; caller-supplied role identity is refused. Reports the current bootstrap state (bootstrap_exception_active / bootstrap_review_missing / bootstrap_exception_consumed). workspace_agent_dispatch is the active supported MCP dispatch surface.

paid_cce.notes: Read-only introspection for the dispatch caller/session identity and bootstrap review contract. Identity authority must be launcher- or transport-minted; caller-supplied role identity is refused. Reports the current bootstrap state (bootstrap_exception_active / bootstrap_review_missing / bootstrap_exception_consumed), and under a valid paid/CCE key posture the graph_impact_persistence_unavailable state for graph-impact evidence persistence prerequisites. workspace_agent_dispatch is the active supported MCP dispatch surface.

tools.notes: Preferred MCP dispatch-readiness surface for a WK or slice. When required graph impact is stale or missing, it refreshes the canonical current-HEAD graph and may write only ignored code-index graph artifacts, sibling atomic temporary files, the advisory build-lock file, and eight exclusively claimed candidate slots named .index.json.build-lock.json.slot-00.candidate through .index.json.build-lock.json.slot-07.candidate. Candidates are attempted only during the initial absent-lock race, retained but never reused or authoritative, and prevented by an existing persistent shared lock; exhaustion falls back to an independent atomic build. It never mutates canonical WK/evidence, admission sidecars, lifecycle or runtime state, dispatch/backend state, or result evidence, and never launches an agent. A bounded current-HEAD resolver failure preserves its safe typed code: verbose readiness includes graph_impact_failure, while compact output includes graph_impact_failure_code and the fixed remediation as next_action; raw causes are not exposed. Compact by default (decision code, bounded reasons, next action); verbose:true restores the full envelope. Free/local readiness covers only the structural runnability floor (write_scope, acceptance, validation present, a supported role, a resolvable subject, a fresh source digest). Per DEC-0123/DEC-0125 a confirmed no-Node-Engine posture renders no local admissibility judgment, so admissibility threshold analysis is not part of free-tier readiness guidance. CLI fallback is operator-only.
do_not_use_when: initiative_next_action before a unit is selected
requires_prior_state: role when validating a role-specific dispatch

paid_cce.notes: Preferred MCP dispatch-readiness surface for a WK or slice. When required graph impact is stale or missing, it refreshes the canonical current-HEAD graph and may write only ignored code-index graph artifacts, sibling atomic temporary files, the advisory build-lock file, and eight exclusively claimed candidate slots named .index.json.build-lock.json.slot-00.candidate through .index.json.build-lock.json.slot-07.candidate. Candidates are attempted only during the initial absent-lock race, retained but never reused or authoritative, and prevented by an existing persistent shared lock; exhaustion falls back to an independent atomic build. It never mutates canonical WK/evidence, admission sidecars, lifecycle or runtime state, dispatch/backend state, or result evidence, and never launches an agent. Compact by default (decision code, bounded reasons, next action); verbose:true restores the full envelope. Under a valid paid/CCE key posture the readiness envelope also carries Node-Engine-returned admissibility detail: blast-radius level, cluster count, and the CCE verdict/reason codes and recovery. These are NE-returned judgments and are reported as such, distinguished from the raw measured carrier facts the local layer forwards; the local layer renders no threshold verdict of its own (DEC-0125). Set node_engine_admissibility:true to evaluate CCE-exclusive implementation admissibility for a structurally dispatchable unit; only the CCE pack path can return an admit and there is no local admit fallback. CLI fallback is operator-only.

tools.notes: Agent-safe MCP route for workers to run declared Node test validation for an implementation unit without raw shell or raw exec. Side effect: process_spawn. Caller input is exactly { unit, target } for the fixed enum command `node_test`; the handler loads the canonical work record/slice for `unit` itself and authorizes `target` solely from that unit's sections.structured_validation.allowed[] entries with command node_test. It then runs `node --check <target>` and, only if check passes, `node --test <target>` using argv arrays with shell:false. Node binary, cwd, env, per-step timeout, and output caps are internal server constants; caller-supplied authority-shaped fields (snapshot, runtime/env policy, node binary, cwd/workspace root, timeout, output cap, source digest, extra args) are rejected. Target must be repo-relative, canonical, existing, .js/.mjs, contained under the workspace repo, and not a symlink escape. Returns structured per-step evidence with node --test reported as skipped when node --check fails. Family-neutral: Codex, Claude, and Agy workers see the same contract. The structured evidence is command-surface validation, not a paid Chassis Control Engine enforcement attestation; arbitrary-command, npm-script, and cross-repo validation remain follow-up scope.
